pattern: have got for possession in the present, preferred in UK speech, esp. questions/negatives (Have you got…? I haven't got…); not for past or actions (have breakfast)
UK option: collective noun (team, family, staff, government) + plural verb when thinking of the members; singular is also correct; keep pronouns plural too (they, their)
exampleGloss: the players of the team are playing well

pattern: present perfect with already/just/yet is the UK norm; US speech often uses the past simple here
exampleGloss: are you still hungry, or did you eat earlier?
